title: Nanoscale linear response of strongly disordered stable solids
authors: D. V. Babin, I. O. Raikov, Y. M. Beltukov
abstract: Strongly disordered solids exhibit distinctive properties at the nanoscale, where conventional continuum theory breaks down. We show that their disorder-averaged linear response can be described by a modified continuum theory in which the response coefficients are local but depend nonlocally on the structural properties. The stability criterion requires the response operator to be positive semidefinite, which naturally leads to a correlated Wishart disorder. In the limit of strong disorder, these equations reduce the long-wavelength response to a scalar disorder-induced contrast field. In elasticity, this field describes the formation of a stiff shell around rigid nanoparticles and boundaries, whose characteristic extent is set by the nonaffine length. The predictions are confirmed by molecular-dynamics simulations of a Lennard-Jones glass and a model polymer. Direct calculation of the nonlocal elastic kernels further shows that the response is predominantly local on the scale of the stiffened interphase.
summary: This work develops a modified continuum theory to describe how strongly disordered solids respond elastically at the nanoscale. It shows that disorder averaging leads to an effective contrast field, which quantifies systematic stiffening around rigid features like nanoparticles. The findings are confirmed via molecular dynamics simulations of glassy materials.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to describe the nanoscale linear response of strongly disordered stable solids where conventional continuum theories fail due to significant spatial heterogeneity.
main_result: The disorder-averaged response can be modeled by a modified continuum theory, which predicts that in the strong disorder limit, the long-wavelength behavior is governed by a scalar disorder-induced contrast field describing stiff shells around inclusions.
method: The approach involves using a disorder-averaged linear response framework applied to the force-constant matrix of the solid, leading to an effective continuum description.
model_or_system: The system studied is amorphous or structurally disordered solids (like glasses or polymers) analyzed near equilibrium. The theory uses elastic response principles derived from minimizing potential energy subject to disorder averaging.
key_observables: Nonlocal Elastic Contrast Field ($\alpha(r)$), which quantifies systematic spatial stiffening; the disorder-averaged linear response coefficients.
important_parameters: The nonaffine length ($\xi$), characterizing the scale of local strain fluctuations, and the temperature regime ($T \ll T_g$).
main_assumptions: The theory relies on a disorder-averaged approach and initially assumes conditions that allow reduction to a scalar contrast field, though generalizations are discussed.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates nonaffine deformation in a 1D chain comparing undeformed, affine, and energy-minimizing nonaffine states. Figure 2 shows spatial stiffening around rigid inclusions due to suppressed nonaffine relaxation.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the need for modified continuum descriptions, deriving equations for the disorder-averaged Green functions, and then solving for the contrast field $\alpha(r)$ which governs the long-wavelength response in the strong disorder limit.
why_interesting: While focused on classical elasticity, the mathematical techniques used—disorder averaging, effective medium theories, and characterizing spatial correlations ($\xi$)—are highly relevant to understanding localization phenomena in quantum systems or modeling complex energy landscapes in AMO physics.

One-dimensional illustration of nonaffine deforma- tion in a chain of particles connected by bonds of unequal stiffness, represented by the thickness and color of the hori- zontal lines. (a) Undeformed chain. (b) Affine deformation, for which all bonds undergo the same relative extension. (c) Energy-minimizing nonaffine deformation at the same total elongation of the chain. The nonaffine displacements relative to the affine configuration are indicated by blue arrows, and the dashed blue lines are visual guides.

FIG. 2. Two-dimensional illustration of the spatial stiffen- ing of an amorphous matrix caused by the suppression of nonaffine deformations near rigid inclusions, as described by Eq. (1). The hatched gray regions represent a planar rigid boundary (A) and two circular inclusions (B, C). The sur- rounding amorphous matrix is colored according to its effec- tive stiffness. The yellow regions correspond to the strongest suppression of nonaffine relaxation and, consequently, to the largest stiffness enhancement. The disorder length is chosen as ξ = R/2, where R is the radius of the circular inclusions.
